Textual reuse data computed by DharmaNexus demonstrates that the *Abyākaraṇīyapañha* shares 228 matching passages across 36 other Pali texts, centering predominantly on canonical treatments of the undetermined questions (*abyākata*) [DharmaNexus]. Major alignments occur with the *Abyākata Saṁyutta* (SN 44, especially §6.10–6.13 sharing phrasing with SN 44.3), the *Dasakanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 10.96), and classic discourses on undeclared matters such as the *Cūḷamālukya Sutta* (MN 63), the *Poṭṭhapāda Sutta* (DN 9), and the *Vacchagotta Saṁyutta* (SN 33) [DharmaNexus]. Further internal reuse is found in Abhidhamma and treatise literature, including the Dhammasaṅgaṇī (*Dukanikkhepa*, Ds 2.3.2), the Paṭisambhidāmagga (*Diṭṭhikathā*, Ps 1.2), the Vibhaṅga (Vb 16 and Vb 17), and the Kathāvatthu (*Abyākatakathā*, Kv 14.8), as well as other sections of the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.2.7, Mil 5.5.2, and Mil 5.5.9) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages with non-Pali works, including the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4090) and the Sanskrit *Dharmasaṃgraha* attributed to Nāgārjuna [DharmaNexus].
